correctness.rationale: At frozen RESULT.md blob 93da3a0dab9ac19bb35f8795ac75bee531c3ae9b, for fixed q>0 the polar change x=r cosφ, y=−r sinφ gives r'=−rS sin²φ and φ'=1−S sinφ cosφ, S=−q+r²[1+(β−1)sin²φ]. Independently verified both polar equations symbolically. At β=1, r=√q is an exact hyperbolic attracting cycle, multiplier e^(−2πq); analytic continuation is licensed for each fixed q. The first radial variation v yields w=2√q v+q sin²φ solving w'+2q sin²φ w=q sin2φ, which has a unique π-periodic solution since homogeneous multiplier e^(−πq)≠1. Differentiation of the ORIGINAL time-period integral gives T_β=1/2∫w sin2φ; multiplying w's equation by w, integrating, gives T_β=∫sin²φ w²>0, because zero would force w≡0 despite nonzero forcing. With w=q z and ∫_0^π sin²φ z=0, the q→0 limit z0=−1/4−(1/2)cos2φ gives exact coefficient ∫_0^(2π) sin²φ z0²=π/16, so T_β=π q²/16+O(q³). All q>0 only pointwise in β-neighborhood, not uniform/global monotonicity. Independent SymPy verification of polar identities and π/16 coefficient; numerical quadrature is not a universal proof.

value.rationale: Period sensitivity is a natural dynamical invariant not determined by knowing exact cycle existence. The exact fact is independently useful for perturbation, stability and oscillator calibration, without requiring global monotonicity or a new phase portrait.
